_comment: Declarative resource manifest for the dashboard's Resources tab.
WHY A MANIFEST: adding a resource should be a data change, not a code change.
The backend executes ONLY what is listed here - a request can name a resource
id but can never supply a command. That is the whole security model, so keep
argv arrays literal and never interpolate anything from a request into them.
command  - run argv, match `expect` (regex, case-insensitive) against stdout
file     - report existence and mode of `path` (~ expanded). NEVER reads content.
check.secret_output: true  -> the detail line is withheld from the API response.
action.command is shown to the operator to run themselves. Actions are NEVER
executed by the server. Anything touching a credential MUST set secret: true,
which makes the UI state plainly that it must be run in a real terminal.

resources.name: Atlassian — Jira + Confluence
resources.summary: Jira is the task system of record; Confluence is the documentation sink. Two paths are both required because MCP cannot be reached from a shell script.

actions.label: Create the REST config
actions.note: Uses getpass: the token is never echoed and never becomes a command argument.

notes: OAuth runs as you, and agents spawn unrestricted, so any agent can close tickets or edit spaces. The MCP server has no read-only variant.
Cloud only — no Server/Data Center, no FedRAMP/HIPAA.
Site rate limits: Free 500 calls/hour, Standard and Premium 1000/hour.

resources.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
resources.summary: Backend/implementation agent. Account auth via ChatGPT OAuth — no API key.
notes: A Windows npm shim on PATH will fail under WSL with 'Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64'. The harness prepends the nvm node bin to avoid it.
codex exec reads stdin — redirect from /dev/null when scripting it.

resources.name: xAI Grok Build CLI
resources.summary: Reviewer/analyst agent. Browser or device-code login to the Grok account; XAI_API_KEY is only the non-browser fallback.
notes: grok -p BLOCKS ON STDIN. Always redirect from /dev/null when scripting it.
Headless runs need --permission-mode bypassPermissions, or a tool-approval prompt nobody can answer cancels the turn.
Usage is billed per request even with browser login.

resources.name: Claude Code (WSL)
resources.summary: Orchestrator and frontend agent. Spawned agents get an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

actions.label: Log in (interactive)
actions.note: Run claude, then /login. Windows keeps its login in the DPAPI credential store, which Linux cannot read — no symlink can share it.

notes: The effective config dir is ~/.claude-wsl via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, not ~/.claude. Add MCP servers with --scope user AND that variable set, or they land at project scope in a file spawned agents never read.

resources.name: agentmux harness
resources.summary: tmux-backed agent orchestration on a dedicated socket.
notes: The launcher exports AGENTMUX_REPO so the harness can find taskmgmt/task.py — it runs via process substitution and cannot locate itself.

resources.name: Voice CLI
resources.summary: Local Whisper push-to-talk that types speech into any CLI window. Windows app in voice-cli/; Claude drives it through the voice-cli plugin in plugins/voice-cli/.

checks.label: running (local API answers)
checks._note: The unauthenticated /health answers only ok, app and version. The dashboard never reads the API token. 47821 is the app's default port.

actions.label: Install the Claude plugin (Windows)
actions.command: claude plugin marketplace add gtownarmy-design/Forktah; claude plugin install voice-cli@forktah

notes: Windows only. The probes cross into Windows with powershell.exe, so they need WSL interop; from a non-WSL Linux box all three report not installed.
The app binds 127.0.0.1 on Windows, which WSL cannot reach under NAT networking, so a Claude running inside WSL cannot use the plugin.

resources.name: Plugins & skills

checks.label: grok plugins installed
checks._note: Matches the name@marketplace listing form. A negative lookahead does NOT work here: re.search with re.M finds a match later in the output and reports a false ok.

actions.label: Install a grok plugin (needs --trust)
actions.note: Plugins can run hooks, MCP servers and skills. --trust is an execute-untrusted-code decision.

notes: Claude plugin metadata records absolute paths. Sharing plugins/known_marketplaces.json between Windows and WSL breaks them — link-windows-state.sh deliberately keeps those two files per-OS.
